original_question: (A. Thom). Is there any group which is not isomorphic to the quotient of a residually finite group by an amenable normal subgroup?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.118 (A. Thom) in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)"
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper's official formulation essentially verbatim: it has the correct attribution to A. Thom, keeps the problem as a pure existence question, and uses the exact quotient condition involving a residually finite group and an amenable normal subgroup.
refined_question: Does there exist a group G such that G is not isomorphic to R/N for any residually finite group R and any amenable normal subgroup N of R?
justification: The cited arXiv item is not a conventional research article with a Section 1 theorem/conjecture setup, but the Kourovka Notebook, a collection of open problems. The draft question is already the exact official statement of Problem 21.118. The surrounding text on the same page adds no extra hypotheses such as finite generation, countability, torsion assumptions, or an equivalent reformulation. The only refinement needed to make it fully stand-alone is to spell out the quantified group variable G and the universal quantification over all pairs (R, N).
